entry.title: Altman on OpenAI's IPO Plans, AI Agent Dots, AI Security
entry.summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman talks about launching its new AI personal agent called Dots, which he says is a premium product. Altman also says the company will go public at some point, but it's being patient. He speaks to Bloomberg's Ed Ludlow in San Francisco. (Source: Bloomberg)

entry.title: Sam Altman Says OpenAI Investors Patient With IPO Plan
entry.summary: CEO Sam Altman says OpenAI ultimately wants to become a public company, but not yet. Speaking with Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg The Close," Altman pushes back on the idea that the responsibilities of being public are incompatible with a focus on safety. (Source: Bloomberg)

entry.title: AMD Goes Big on World Models as Anthropic Heads to IPO
entry.summary: Bloomberg’s Ed Ludlow breaks down President Trump's new AI-powered website America.gov, putting AI at the center of his agenda. Plus, Anthropic warns of "existential risks to humanity" in its prospectus ahead of its IPO according to reports, and AMD makes a big AI bet on the frontier by acquiring Fei-Fei Li's World Labs in an all-stock deal valued at $8.2 billion. (Source: Bloomberg)

entry.title: Goldman Sachs expects Big Tech to spend $1.2 trillion on AI infrastructure by 2027, dwarfing Wall Street estimates
entry.summary: Goldman Sachs projects that Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft, Oracle, and Meta will pour a combined $1.2 trillion into AI infrastructure in 2027, more than 50 percent above this year's levels. Measured against GDP, it would be the biggest investment cycle since railroad construction in the 19th century. Bottlenecks in power, labor, and memory chips could slow the pace, though.
